title: Ethiopian Chilli Vinegar
community: Ethiopian restaurants — the table condiment vinegar
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Chilli Vinegar — white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar infused with dried bird's eye chillies, garlic, and berbere spices. The table condiment served at Ethiopian restaurants — used to add acid and heat to dishes.
longDesc: Chilli vinegar is the modern Ethiopian restaurant's table condiment — the acid element that provides a different heat experience from awaze and adds brightness to any Ethiopian dish.
ingredients: 1 cup white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar
steps: Place chillies, garlic, and berbere in a clean bottle.
Infuse at room temperature for 5—7 days before use.
chefTips: Red wine vinegar produces a more complex flavour; white is more neutral.
1 week minimum infusion — the chilli heat needs time to fully infuse.
cookingScience: Acetic acid in vinegar extracts the water-soluble capsaicin compounds from the chilli more efficiently than oil. Over 5—7 days, the capsaicin concentration in the vinegar reaches equilibrium with the chilli flesh.
sustainabilityTips: Apple cider vinegar is the most sustainable choice — produced from fermented apples with minimal processing.
servedWith: As a table condiment on any Ethiopian dish
storage: Indefinitely at room temperature — the acidity prevents spoilage.
culturalNote: Chilli vinegar is the modern Ethiopian restaurant's condiment table addition — providing the acid and heat element that complements the rich, fat-based sauces.
